Accountable obligation owner.value: Plan Controller owns the ERISA plan financial statements (Schedule H Parts I and II) and the large-plan IQPA opinion attachment; escalation to the Chief Financial Officer as Plan Administrator delegate

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — ERISA §103(a)(3), 29 U.S.C. §1023(a)(3) and ERISA §102 / 29 CFR 2520.102-3 re-read against the current-year EBSA Form 5500 Instructions (Schedule H line 3 audit-opinion coding) at the start of each plan-year close

In-scope processes.value: Plan-year financial close for every ERISA plan with 100+ participants with account balances at the start of the plan year — trust reconciliation, contribution and distribution cut-off, Schedule H balance sheet and income statement build, IQPA opinion attachment

In-scope systems.value: Plan trial balance and sponsor contribution accruals in the GL, reconciled to recordkeeper trust statements; the assembled Schedule H financials are attached in EFAST2 IFILE

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Plan Financial Statement Preparation Procedure — participant-count test at first day of plan year, trust-to-GL reconciliation, Schedule H line mapping, accrual vs cash basis election, IQPA opinion type coding on Schedule H line 3a-3d

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and the plan's Retirement Committee; re-approved each year after EBSA publishes the revised Form 5500 Instructions and Schedule H changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly trust reconciliations at each plan-quarter end; draft plan financial statements to the IQPA within 90 days of plan year end; final audited statements attached to the Form 5500 by the last day of the 7th month after plan year end (July 31 for calendar-year plans), or October 15 with a timely Form 5558

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close calendar alerts at plan year end +45 days (trust recon complete), +90 days (draft statements to IQPA), +150 days (opinion received), and 15 days before the 5500 due date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed plan financial statements, trust-to-GL reconciliations, Schedule H line workpapers and the IQPA opinion retained at least 6 years from the Form 5500 filing date per ERISA §107, and longer where a participant benefit claim may still turn on the record

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A large-plan filing lodged without the auditor's report, an unreconciled trust difference over the audit threshold, or a Schedule H line restated after filing is logged as a compliance exception with root cause and an amended-return decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off any restatement of plan financial statements, any amended Form 5500 filed to add or correct the IQPA report, and the corrective action on any unreconciled trust variance

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every ERISA plan in the sponsor's plan inventory for the plan year, with its participant count at the first day of the plan year, its filer status (large/small), and its filed Schedule H or Schedule I

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any large plan whose Form 5500 was filed without an attached IQPA report is a fail; any trust-to-GL difference above 0.5% of plan net assets left unexplained is a fail; any Schedule H line not traceable to the audited statements is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Quarterly test of the trust-to-GL reconciliation for the largest three plans; full annual test of participant counts, filer status and IQPA attachment across 100% of plans before the 5500 due date

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or reviewed any plan trial balance, Schedule H workpaper or reconciliation in the tested year

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual ERISA plan reporting test workpaper (plan inventory, participant-count extract, Schedule H tie-out, EFAST2 acknowledgement IDs) filed in the compliance evidence repository under the plan year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: For each plan: filed Form 5500 with Schedule H, the IQPA opinion, the audited financial statements and the trust-to-GL reconciliation, producible for an EBSA reporting-compliance inquiry within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: EBSA correspondence (rejection letters, Reporting Compliance Notices) routes to the Controller with Legal Counsel; a rejected large-plan filing is corrected by amended Form 5500 with the IQPA report attached, and DFVCP is evaluated where the filing is treated as not filed

checklist.step: Run the first-day participant count and set each plan's filer status
actions: Ask the Retirement Recordkeeping Specialist for the recordkeeper's participant census as of the first day of the plan year — active participants, retirees and beneficiaries receiving benefits, and separated participants with an account balance.
In the HRIS run the benefits eligibility report for the same date and reconcile head counts to the recordkeeper census; investigate any difference over 25 participants before proceeding.
Apply the 100-participants-with-account-balances test and, where the count is between 80 and 120, apply the 80-120 rule to keep the prior year's filer status and write down the election.
Record for every plan on the plan inventory: plan number (001, 002…), EIN, plan year end, first-day count, filer status LARGE or SMALL, and audit required Y/N.
Send the completed inventory to the Controller and the IQPA engagement partner as the trigger for audit scoping.
checklist.done: every plan in the inventory carries a first-day participant count reconciled to the recordkeeper census and a documented large/small filer status.

checklist.step: Pull the trust statements and build the plan trial balance
actions: Download from the recordkeeper/trustee the certified trust statement for the plan year: beginning net assets, contributions received, benefit payments, investment income, realized and unrealized appreciation, and administrative expenses paid from plan assets.
Post the plan trial balance in the GL plan company code and map every trust line to a GL account.
Request from the Payroll Specialist the payroll register totals for employee deferrals, loan repayments and employer match remitted during the plan year.
Reconcile payroll-side remittances to trust-side contribution receipts by pay period and list every difference with an explanation.
Where the trustee issues a certification under 29 CFR 2520.103-5, save the signed certification — it is what supports a §103(a)(3)(C) limited-scope-style audit.
checklist.done: the plan trial balance is posted, tied to the certified trust statement, and every payroll-to-trust remittance difference is explained in writing.

checklist.step: Reconcile trust assets to the GL and clear differences
actions: Open the plan net-assets reconciliation template in the close tool and load the trust ending balance and the GL ending balance.
Break the difference into timing items (contributions in transit, distributions issued but uncashed, pending trades) and true differences.
Chase every true difference over 0.5% of plan net assets with the Retirement Operations Administrator and the trustee until it clears or becomes a booked adjustment.
Attach the trust statement, the GL balance report and the supporting emails to the reconciliation and submit it for Controller approval.
Escalate any uncleared difference to the Controller with an assessment of whether it is a prohibited transaction or a delinquent contribution.
checklist.done: the net-assets reconciliation is approved with zero unexplained difference above 0.5% of plan net assets.

checklist.step: Test contribution timeliness and quantify any delinquent participant contributions
actions: Export every payroll cycle in the plan year with the deferral withholding date and the amount withheld.
Match each cycle to the trust deposit date on the recordkeeper contribution report and compute the days between withholding and deposit.

Flag any deposit later than the earliest date the amounts could reasonably be segregated from general assets (the 7-business-day safe harbor for plans under 100 participants is not available to large plans).
For each late cycle compute lost earnings using the DOL Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program Online Calculator and hand the schedule to the Controller for Schedule H line 4a reporting.
Give the completed timeliness schedule to the Benefits Administrator so the corrective deposit is made and the participants are made whole.
checklist.done: a payroll-cycle timeliness schedule exists with days-to-deposit per cycle and a lost-earnings calculation for every late remittance.

checklist.step: Map the trial balance onto Schedule H Part I and Part II lines
actions: Build the Schedule H tie-out workbook with one column per Schedule H line and one row per GL account.

Populate Part I lines 1a-1l (cash, receivables, general and participant-directed investments, employer securities, buildings) and lines 1g-1k for liabilities, agreeing total net assets to the reconciliation.

Populate Part II lines 2a-2t: employer contributions, participant contributions, non-cash contributions, interest and dividends, net appreciation, benefit payments, corrective distributions, deemed distributions of participant loans, and administrative expenses split between professional fees, contract administrator fees and investment advisory fees.
Enter line 4a delinquent participant contributions from the payroll timeliness schedule and line 4j reportable transactions from the 5% schedule.
Foot and cross-foot the workbook so beginning net assets plus net income equals ending net assets, and circulate it to the IQPA as the audit tie-out.
checklist.done: every Schedule H Part I and Part II line traces to a GL account in the tie-out workbook and the roll-forward balances to the dollar.

checklist.step: Draft the plan financial statements in the ERISA presentation
actions: Draft the Statement of Net Assets Available for Benefits and the Statement of Changes in Net Assets Available for Benefits for the current and prior plan year.

Draft the notes: plan description, funding policy, vesting schedule, participant loans, investment valuation and fair value hierarchy levels, tax status with the IRS determination or opinion letter date, party-in-interest transactions, and risks and uncertainties.
State the basis of accounting (accrual) and disclose any difference between the financial statements and Form 5500 Schedule H amounts in a reconciling note.
Circulate the draft to the Compensation & Benefits Manager to confirm the plan-provision narrative matches the current plan document and amendments.
Save the numbered draft into the financial reporting repository under plan number and plan year.
checklist.done: a complete draft financial statement set with notes exists, agreed to the Schedule H tie-out and to the current plan document.

checklist.step: Assemble the audit request package for the independent qualified public accountant
actions: Load the IQPA's prepared-by-client list into the audit workspace with an owner and due date on every item.

Upload the plan document and all amendments, the adoption agreement, the IRS determination or opinion letter, the trust agreement, the recordkeeping and investment management agreements, and the current fidelity bond.
Upload the certified trust statement, trial balance, Schedule H tie-out, participant census, payroll registers and the contribution timeliness schedule.
Obtain the recordkeeper's SOC 1 Type 2 report covering the plan year and confirm the report period covers the full 12 months, noting any gap period that needs a bridge letter.
Track open items daily and escalate anything unanswered for more than five business days to the Controller.
checklist.done: the IQPA prepared-by-client list is 100% delivered, including a SOC 1 Type 2 covering the whole plan year or a bridge letter for the gap.

checklist.step: Set the audit scope election and confirm the certification supports it
actions: Decide whether the plan will take an ERISA §103(a)(3)(C) audit and document the basis: assets held by a qualifying bank or insurance carrier that certifies both completeness and accuracy.
Read the certification letter and confirm it is signed by an authorised officer of the qualifying institution and covers the full plan-year investment information.
Confirm with the Compensation & Benefits Manager that management is willing to make the written §103(a)(3)(C) permissibility acknowledgement the auditor requires under AU-C 703.
Where any asset class is not certified (self-directed brokerage, real estate, employer securities), scope it into full audit testing and tell the IQPA.
Record the election and its support on the audit scoping memo.
checklist.done: the audit scope election is documented, supported by a qualifying certification, and non-certified asset classes are explicitly scoped in.

checklist.step: Clear audit findings and post agreed adjustments
actions: Log every proposed audit adjustment and every reportable finding from the IQPA on the audit issues list with an owner.
Post agreed adjustments to the plan trial balance and re-run the Schedule H tie-out so the workbook and the statements move together.

For findings that are operational failures (late deposits, incorrect compensation definition, missed deferral opportunity), open a correction under EPCRS with the Benefits Administrator and record the correction method.
Update the notes for any subsequent event through the report date.
Confirm in writing to the IQPA that no further adjustments are outstanding before the opinion is issued.
checklist.done: the audit issues list is closed, adjustments are posted, and the tie-out and statements agree after adjustment.

checklist.step: Obtain the signed IQPA opinion and classify its type
actions: Receive the manually signed audit report on the accounting firm's letterhead, dated, with the city and state of the office issuing it.
Classify the opinion as unmodified, qualified, adverse or disclaimer, and separately note whether it is an ERISA §103(a)(3)(C) audit report.
Map the classification to Form 5500 Schedule H line 3a (opinion type) and line 3b, and record the accountant's name, EIN and address for line 3c.
Where the opinion is other than unmodified, brief the Chief Financial Officer and the Retirement Committee on the cause before the filing goes out.
File the signed opinion PDF with the financial statements as a single attachment ready for EFAST2.
checklist.done: a signed, dated IQPA report exists, its opinion type is classified, and the Schedule H line 3 coding is set from it.

checklist.step: Present the plan financial statements to the Retirement Committee for approval
actions: Circulate the audited statements, the IQPA opinion, the auditor's governance communication letter and the Schedule H tie-out to the Retirement Committee at least five business days before the meeting.
Walk the committee through net assets, contributions, benefit payments, expenses paid from plan assets and any line 4a delinquent contributions.
Record the committee's approval resolution, the attendees and the date in the minutes.
Capture any committee action item (fee benchmarking, deposit process fix) with an owner and a due date.
checklist.done: committee minutes record approval of the audited plan financial statements with attendees, date and any assigned action items.

checklist.step: Attach the audited statements and opinion to the Form 5500 in EFAST2
actions: Open the plan's Form 5500 in EFAST2 IFILE and go to Schedule H, then the Accountant's Opinion attachment slot.
Attach the audited financial statements, notes, supplemental schedules and the signed IQPA report as a single searchable PDF named per the EFAST2 attachment convention.
Complete Schedule H lines 3a-3d from the opinion classification worksheet and confirm line 3d(2) is only used where an ERISA §103(a)(3)(C) audit applies.
Run the EFAST2 validation and clear every error and warning — a large-plan filing with no accountant's opinion attached will be treated as incomplete and rejected.
Record the filing in the regulatory reporting log with the plan number, EIN, plan year and attachment file name.
checklist.done: the audited statements and signed opinion are attached to Schedule H in EFAST2 and the filing passes validation with no outstanding errors.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filed Schedule H back to the audited statements after submission
actions: Download the accepted Form 5500 PDF from EFAST2 using the acknowledgement ID.
Compare Schedule H line by line to the audited Statement of Net Assets and Statement of Changes, including line 4a, 4j and the expense split.
Where any line differs, decide same day whether an amended Form 5500 is required and record the decision and its basis.
Store the accepted filing PDF and the acknowledgement ID alongside the audited statements in the evidence folder.
checklist.done: the filed Schedule H is reconciled line-for-line to the audited statements and the acknowledgement ID is stored with the evidence.

checklist.step: Run the interim quarterly reconciliation between annual cycles
actions: At each plan-quarter end, reconcile trust net assets to the GL plan trial balance using the same template as the annual reconciliation.
Re-run the payroll-to-trust contribution timeliness test for the quarter's pay cycles so a late-deposit pattern is caught inside the year, not at audit.
Report to the Controller any quarter-over-quarter movement in net assets over 10% with the driver identified (market, large distribution, plan merger).
Submit the quarterly reconciliation for Controller approval within 30 days of the quarter end.
checklist.done: an approved trust-to-GL reconciliation and contribution timeliness test exists for every plan quarter within 30 days of quarter end.

checklist.step: Archive the plan-year financial reporting record under ERISA retention
actions: Move the plan-year package — audited statements, IQPA opinion, Schedule H tie-out, reconciliations, census, trustee certification, committee minutes and the accepted EFAST2 filing — into the repository under plan number and plan year.
Apply the ERISA §107 retention label of at least 6 years from the filing date, and the longer §209 label where the record supports individual benefit entitlement.
Confirm the repository index makes the package searchable by EIN, plan number, plan year and EFAST2 acknowledgement ID.
Give the Controller and Internal Auditor read access for the next cycle's testing.
checklist.done: the plan-year package is archived, labelled for ERISA retention and retrievable by EIN, plan number and acknowledgement ID.

testing.step: Build the population of ERISA plans and their filer status
actions: Extract every benefit plan flagged as ERISA-covered from the HRIS plan table with EIN, plan number, plan year end and plan type.
Add plans acquired or merged during the year from the corporate development close checklist so short-plan-year filings cannot be missed.
Reconcile the plan list to the prior-year EFAST2 filing history retrieved by EIN so no plan silently drops out of the population.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and record counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: the plan population is reconciled to prior-year EFAST2 filings and to the acquisition list, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Re-perform the first-day participant count and the large-plan determination
actions: Pull the recordkeeper census file as of the first day of the plan year directly from the recordkeeper portal rather than from the preparer's copy.
Recount participants with account balances and compare to the count recorded on the plan inventory.
Recompute the large/small determination and, where the 80-120 rule was used, confirm the prior-year filer status and that the election was applied consistently.
Treat any plan mis-classified as small when it had 100+ participants with balances as a critical exception — that filing is missing a required audit.
testing.done: the participant count and filer status are independently recomputed for every plan and every difference is logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of plans and Schedule H lines
actions: Take 100% of large plans and 100% of plans whose filer status changed from the prior year.
Take a seeded random sample of 5 small plans to test that the small-plan classification held.
Within each sampled plan select Schedule H lines 1a-1l totals, 2a, 2e, 2i, 4a and 4j for tie-out.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and sample rationale so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample covers 100% of large plans, is reproducible from a recorded seed, and names the Schedule H lines tested.

testing.step: Confirm an IQPA report is attached to every large-plan filing
actions: For each sampled large plan retrieve the accepted Form 5500 from EFAST2 by acknowledgement ID.
Open the Accountant's Opinion attachment and confirm it is a manually signed report on firm letterhead, dated, naming the plan and the plan year.
Compare the firm name, EIN and address in the attachment to Schedule H line 3c and the opinion type to line 3a.
Any large-plan filing with no attachment, an unsigned report, or a mismatch between the attached opinion type and line 3a is an automatic fail.
testing.done: every sampled large-plan filing carries a signed IQPA report whose firm details and opinion type agree with Schedule H line 3.

testing.step: Tie the filed Schedule H lines to the audited financial statements
actions: Enter the selected Schedule H line amounts from the accepted filing into the test workbook.
Enter the corresponding figures from the audited Statement of Net Assets and Statement of Changes.
Compute the variance on every line and require a written reconciling explanation for any variance, however small.
Confirm beginning net assets plus net income equals ending net assets on the filed schedule.
testing.done: every tested Schedule H line agrees to the audited statements or has a documented reconciling explanation, and the roll-forward foots.

testing.step: Re-perform the trust-to-GL reconciliation for the largest plans
actions: Obtain the certified trust statement direct from the trustee or recordkeeper portal for the three largest plans by net assets.
Pull the GL plan trial balance for the same date and independently compute the difference.
Vouch each reconciling item to source: contributions in transit to the payroll register, uncashed distribution checks to the disbursement register, pending trades to the trade confirmations.
Flag any residual unexplained difference above 0.5% of plan net assets as a fail against the stated threshold.
testing.done: the reconciliation is independently recomputed for the three largest plans with every reconciling item vouched to source.

testing.step: Recompute contribution timeliness and the line 4a disclosure
actions: Select 15 payroll cycles across the plan year, weighted toward quarter-ends and any month with an off-cycle payroll.
Recompute days between deferral withholding and trust deposit from the payroll register date and the trust posting date.
Recompute lost earnings on any late cycle using the DOL VFCP Online Calculator and compare to the amount deposited.
Compare the total delinquent participant contributions you compute to the amount reported on Schedule H line 4a and log any understatement.
testing.done: days-to-deposit and lost earnings are independently recomputed for 15 cycles and reconcile to the amount reported on line 4a.

testing.step: Test the §103(a)(3)(C) scope election and the SOC 1 coverage
actions: For each sampled plan taking a §103(a)(3)(C) audit, read the institution's certification and confirm it covers both completeness and accuracy and is signed by an authorised officer.
Confirm the certifying institution is a bank, similar institution or insurance carrier regulated and supervised and subject to periodic examination.
Check that non-certified asset classes (self-directed brokerage windows, real estate, employer securities) were scoped into full testing rather than excluded.

Obtain the recordkeeper SOC 1 Type 2 and confirm the period covers the whole plan year or a bridge letter closes the gap; list all complementary user entity controls and confirm the sponsor operates them.
testing.done: each scope election is supported by a qualifying signed certification, non-certified assets are scoped in, and SOC 1 coverage plus user entity controls are evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording plan number, plan year, the Schedule H line or control affected, and the dollar impact.
Assign a root cause — census cut-off error, filer-status misjudgement, unreconciled trust item, late deferral deposits, missing audit attachment — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the filing itself is defective, record the amended Form 5500 decision and its target filing date.
Refer late-deposit findings to Legal Counsel for a VFCP and Form 5330 excise tax assessment, and carry every open issue into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, an amended-filing decision where relevant, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the plan financial reporting test
actions: Compute the exception rate by plan and by Schedule H line tested against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no trial balance, reconciliation or Schedule H workpaper in the tested year, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any missing-audit findings to the Retirement Committee and the Audit Committee at their next sittings and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an exception rate, a stated conclusion and a dated committee reporting reference is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns on-time submission of the Form 5500 series and the participant disclosure deadlines for every ERISA plan; escalation to the Corporate Secretary as the named Plan Administrator

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l), 29 CFR 2578.1 and the EBSA Cybersecurity Program Best Practices / Compliance Assistance Release 2021-01 re-read against the current EFAST2 filing instructions before each plan-year filing window opens

In-scope processes.value: Annual Form 5500 / 5500-SF submission through EFAST2, Form 5558 extension requests, Form 8955-SSA to the IRS, PBGC premium filings for defined benefit plans, and the participant disclosure clock (SPD within 120 days of a plan becoming subject to ERISA, within 90 days of a participant first covered, documents on written request within 30 days)

In-scope systems.value: EFAST2 IFILE for the Form 5500 series with credentials held under DOL-issued filing signer IDs; filing status, acknowledgement IDs and deadline evidence mirrored into the internal regulatory reporting log

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Filing and Disclosure Submission Procedure — filer role assignment, EFAST2 credential custody, extension decision rule, signature authority, validation-error clearance and acknowledgement capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Corporate Secretary; re-approved annually and whenever EBSA changes the EFAST2 signature or credential rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Form 5500 due the last day of the 7th month after plan year end (July 31 for calendar-year plans), extended to October 15 by a Form 5558 filed on or before the original due date; Summary Annual Report to participants within 9 months of plan year end or 2 months after the extended due date; SPD within 120 days of the plan becoming subject to ERISA and within 90 days of a participant first being covered; requested documents furnished within 30 days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts at plan year end +150 days (draft package), 30 days before the original due date (extension go/no-go), 10 and 3 business days before each of July 31 and October 15, and at the SAR and 30-day document-request clocks

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: EFAST2 acknowledgement IDs and filing receipts, Form 5558 confirmations, SAR distribution logs and 30-day document-request response logs retained 6 years from filing date under ERISA §107

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any filing submitted after its due date, any filing rejected by EFAST2 validation, and any document request answered later than 30 days is logged with root cause and a DFVCP or §502(c) penalty exposure assessment

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or amended Form 5500, every DFVCP submission, and the corrective distribution plan for any missed participant disclosure

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on statutory filing dates — one filing after its due date without a timely Form 5558 is a fail; any document request answered after 30 days is a fail given §502(c)(1) exposure of up to $110 per day per participant

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Annual full-population test after the October 15 extended deadline closes, plus a quarterly test of the 30-day document-request log because that clock runs continuously

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must hold no EFAST2 filing signer credential and must not have prepared or submitted any tested filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual ERISA filing timeliness workpaper (filing inventory, EFAST2 acknowledgement extract, extension confirmations, SAR distribution proof) in the compliance evidence repository under the plan year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per plan: EFAST2 acknowledgement ID and receipt, Form 5558 confirmation, filed Form 5500 PDF, SAR distribution log and postal/electronic delivery proof, producible for an EBSA or IRS inquiry within 5 business days

checklist.step: Build the plan-year filing calendar from the plan inventory
actions: Load every ERISA plan from the plan inventory into the filing calendar with EIN, three-digit plan number, plan year end and plan type (defined contribution, defined benefit, welfare).
Compute each plan's original Form 5500 due date as the last day of the 7th month after its plan year end and the extended date as 2½ months later.
Add the dependent deadlines to each plan row: Form 8955-SSA, PBGC premium filing for DB plans, and the Summary Annual Report to participants.
Assign a named preparer, a named reviewer and a DOL-credentialed filing signer to each plan row.
Send the calendar to the Corporate Secretary and the Controller for confirmation that the named Plan Administrator on each row matches the plan document.
checklist.done: every plan has a calendar row with original and extended due dates, dependent deadlines, and named preparer, reviewer and filing signer.

checklist.step: Verify EFAST2 credentials and signature authority before the window opens
actions: Confirm each filing signer holds a current EFAST2 user ID with the Filing Signer role registered under their own name and email — credentials are personal and must never be shared.
Have any signer whose credentials have lapsed re-register at the EFAST2 website and complete the electronic signature agreement before the package is ready.
Confirm the Plan Administrator signer and, where the plan is funded through a trust, the Plan Sponsor signer are both provisioned.

Apply the EBSA Cybersecurity Program Best Practices (Compliance Assistance Release 2021-01) controls to the credential store: MFA enforced, no shared mailboxes, access reviewed each quarter with the Access Management Analyst.
Record credential status per plan row on the filing calendar.
checklist.done: every plan row shows an active, individually-held EFAST2 filing signer credential with MFA, verified before the filing window opens.

checklist.step: Assemble the Form 5500 package and its required schedules
actions: Open the plan's return in EFAST2 IFILE and complete Part I and Part II of the Form 5500: plan name, plan number, EIN, plan year dates, participant counts and the plan characteristic codes.

Attach the schedules the plan requires — Schedule A for insurance contracts, C for service provider fees, D for DFE participation, G for non-exempt transactions, H or I for financials, R for retirement plan distributions, SB or MB for actuarial information.
Pull the Schedule H figures from the Controller's tie-out workbook and the Schedule A data from each insurance carrier's annual report to the plan.
Chase any carrier that has not delivered its Schedule A information — the carrier is obliged under ERISA §103(a)(2) to supply it, and its absence blocks the filing.
Save the draft return and circulate the IFILE print preview to the named reviewer.
checklist.done: the return is complete in IFILE with every required schedule attached and all carrier-sourced Schedule A data received.

checklist.step: Make the extension decision and file Form 5558 if needed
actions: Thirty days before each plan's original due date, review the package status: audit opinion received, Schedule A data in, reviewer sign-off complete.
Where any of those is outstanding, file Form 5558 Application for Extension of Time with the IRS on or before the original due date — a Form 5558 filed even one day late gives no extension at all.

Complete Form 5558 with the plan name, EIN, plan number, plan year end and the extended date requested (2½ months), and file it electronically where available or mail it to the IRS address in the current instructions with proof of mailing.
Update the plan's calendar row to the extended date and re-arm the reminders.
File the extension confirmation or certified mail receipt in the plan evidence folder — it is the only defence to a late-filing penalty.
checklist.done: every plan needing more time has a Form 5558 filed on or before its original due date with the confirmation retained.

checklist.step: Run EFAST2 validation and clear every error and warning
actions: Run the IFILE validation on the completed return and export the error and warning list.
Fix each error at source — participant-count mismatches go back to the Benefits Analyst, financial line errors to the Controller, actuarial schedule errors to the Actuary.
For each warning left unfixed, write a one-line justification on the filing checklist so the reviewer sees a deliberate decision rather than an oversight.
Re-run validation until the error count is zero, then print the validation report to PDF for the evidence folder.
Confirm the accountant's opinion attachment is present for every large plan — its absence makes the filing incomplete and rejectable.
checklist.done: validation returns zero errors, every remaining warning has a written justification, and the validation report is filed.

checklist.step: Obtain the reviewer sign-off before signature
actions: Review the IFILE print preview against the prior-year filing and question every year-over-year movement over 15% in participant counts, contributions or net assets.
Confirm the plan characteristic codes match the plan document features (auto-enrolment, Roth, safe harbor, participant loans).

Confirm the service provider list on Schedule C reconciles to the fee disclosures received under 29 CFR 2550.408b-2 and that indirect compensation is reported or the alternative reporting option conditions are met.
Sign the filing checklist with name and date, and return any item requiring rework with a same-week due date.
checklist.done: the filing checklist carries a dated reviewer signature and every year-over-year movement over 15% is explained.

checklist.step: Electronically sign and submit through EFAST2
actions: Log in to EFAST2 IFILE under your own filing signer credential — never under another person's ID.
Read the signer attestation, apply the electronic signature as Plan Administrator, and add the Plan Sponsor signature where the plan requires it.
Submit the return and wait for the status to move from Processing to Filed or Filed with Errors.
Capture the acknowledgement ID, submission date and time stamp, and the filing status onto the plan calendar row.
Where the status returns Filed with Errors, treat it as unresolved and hand it straight back to the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day.
checklist.done: the return shows status Filed in EFAST2 with the acknowledgement ID and time stamp recorded against the plan row.

checklist.step: File Form 8955-SSA and the PBGC premium filing on their own clocks
actions: Build the Form 8955-SSA population from the recordkeeper's deferred vested terminated participant report — separated participants with a deferred vested benefit not yet paid.
File Form 8955-SSA with the IRS by the same due date as the Form 5500 (extended by a timely Form 5558) and record the participant count reported.
For each defined benefit plan, complete the PBGC comprehensive premium filing in My PAA with the flat-rate and variable-rate premium calculation and file it by October 15 for calendar-year plans.
Reconcile the premium funding target and participant count used in My PAA to the Schedule SB signed by the Enrolled Actuary.
Save the IRS and PBGC confirmations to the plan evidence folder.
checklist.done: Form 8955-SSA and every PBGC premium filing are submitted by their due dates with confirmations retained and reconciled to Schedule SB.

checklist.step: Distribute the Summary Annual Report inside its window
actions: Prepare the SAR from the filed Schedule H/I figures using the model language in 29 CFR 2520.104b-10, including the notice of the right to receive the full annual report on request.
Build the distribution list of participants and beneficiaries receiving benefits from the HRIS and the recordkeeper census.
Distribute within 9 months of the plan year end, or within 2 months after the extended Form 5500 due date where Form 5558 was filed (December 15 for a calendar-year plan on extension).
Where electronic delivery is used, confirm the safe harbor conditions are met — work-related computer access or affirmative consent, plus the notice of internet availability.
Retain the distribution log with dates, delivery channel, recipient counts and bounce-back handling.
checklist.done: the SAR is distributed inside the 9-month or extended 2-month window with a retained log showing dates, channel and recipient counts.

checklist.step: Serve participant document requests inside the 30-day clock
actions: Log every written request for plan documents — SPD, latest annual report, plan document, trust agreement, bargaining agreement — with the received date and a 30-day due date.
Furnish the requested documents within 30 days of the written request as required by ERISA §104(b)(4), and record the send date and channel.
Where a reasonable copying charge is applied, disclose it in advance and keep it within the schedule permitted by 29 CFR 2520.104b-30.
Escalate to Legal Counsel any request that arrives from a participant's attorney or alongside a claim, given §502(c)(1) daily penalty exposure.
Close the case only when the documents are evidenced as sent.
checklist.done: every written document request is closed with a send date inside 30 days of receipt and the evidence attached to the case.

checklist.step: Meet the SPD delivery clocks for new plans and new participants
actions: For any newly established plan, calendar the SPD delivery date at 120 days after the plan becomes subject to ERISA per 29 CFR 2520.104b-2.
Configure the HRIS onboarding workflow so a newly covered participant is issued the SPD within 90 days of first coverage.
Run a monthly exception report of participants whose coverage start date is more than 90 days old with no SPD delivery record, and clear it inside the month.
Track Summary of Material Modifications delivery within 210 days after the plan year in which the amendment was adopted.
Keep the delivery evidence — mail file, electronic delivery receipts and consent records — against each participant record.
checklist.done: no participant is more than 90 days into coverage without an SPD delivery record and every new plan has a 120-day SPD delivery date met.

checklist.step: Handle an abandoned or terminating plan through the qualified termination administrator route
actions: Where a plan sponsor has ceased to exist or cannot be located, assess the abandoned plan criteria in 29 CFR 2578.1 with the Corporate Secretary.
Confirm the qualified termination administrator status of the custodian and have it file the notice of plan abandonment with EBSA within the regulation's timeframe.
Ensure the QTA notifies participants of the termination, the distribution options and the deadline to elect, and that the special terminal report is filed instead of a full Form 5500.
Document the wind-up decisions, the QTA correspondence and the final distribution register in the plan legal file.
checklist.done: any abandoned or terminating plan has a documented 29 CFR 2578.1 assessment, QTA notices and the special terminal report filed.

checklist.step: Capture the acknowledgement evidence and close the filing calendar row
actions: Download the accepted filing PDF and the acknowledgement receipt from EFAST2 for every plan.
Attach the acknowledgement ID, submission timestamp, Form 5558 confirmation, validation report and signer name to the plan's calendar row.
Mark the row Closed-On Time or Closed-Late with the day count against the statutory date — never Closed without a date comparison.
Move the complete filing package into the compliance evidence repository under EIN, plan number and plan year with a 6-year ERISA §107 retention label.
checklist.done: every calendar row is closed with an acknowledgement ID, a timeliness verdict against the statutory date, and the package archived.

checklist.step: Cure any late or rejected filing through DFVCP before EBSA acts
actions: Within one business day of identifying a missed or rejected filing, confirm with Legal Counsel whether the plan remains eligible for the Delinquent Filer Voluntary Compliance Program — eligibility ends once EBSA issues a notice of failure to file.
Complete the delinquent filing in EFAST2 first, then submit the DFVCP application and pay the applicable per-plan penalty through the DFVCP online calculator and payment portal.
Notify the Chief Financial Officer and the Retirement Committee of the exposure and the cure path in writing.
Record the DFVCP acknowledgement in the filing calendar row and the issue tracker, and set the root-cause remediation date.
checklist.done: every late or rejected filing has a completed EFAST2 submission, a DFVCP acknowledgement where eligible, and a written committee notification.

checklist.step: Report filing timeliness to the Retirement Committee each cycle
actions: Publish the cycle dashboard: filings due, filed on time, filed on extension, filed late, rejected, and open document requests past 30 days.
Show each late item with its day count, the penalty exposure and the cure status.
Present the dashboard to the Retirement Committee and record the minute reference.
Roll every unresolved item forward as an open action with an owner and a due date rather than closing the cycle over it.
checklist.done: the committee minutes record the timeliness dashboard, and every late or open item carries a named owner and due date.

testing.step: Build the population of filings due for the plan year
actions: Extract the filing calendar for the plan year with every Form 5500 series, Form 8955-SSA, PBGC premium and SAR obligation.
Independently derive each plan's statutory due date from its plan year end rather than trusting the calendar's stored date.
Add plans that were terminated, merged or newly established mid-year so short-plan-year and final filings enter the population.
Reconcile the population to the EFAST2 filing history for the sponsor's EINs and sign it as complete.
testing.done: the filing population is independently date-derived, reconciled to EFAST2 filing history and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to accepted EFAST2 acknowledgements
actions: Match each population row to an EFAST2 acknowledgement ID on EIN plus plan number plus plan year.
Confirm the filing status is Filed and not Filed with Errors or Processing.
List every unmatched row and every Filed-with-Errors status as an automatic exception with no further judgement.
Capture the EFAST2 filing history screen into the workpaper as the source of the match.
testing.done: every obligation is matched to an accepted acknowledgement ID or listed as an exception, with the source screen captured.

testing.step: Draw and document the timeliness sample
actions: Take 100% of filings submitted within 5 days of a statutory date, all filings on extension, and all late or rejected filings.
Take a seeded random sample of 15 remaining filings and 20 participant document requests from the case log.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and stratification rationale in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample includes at least one filing from each plan type — defined contribution, defined benefit and welfare.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed, covers all near-deadline, extended and late filings, and spans every plan type.

testing.step: Recompute each statutory due date and the extension arithmetic
actions: Recompute the original due date as the last day of the 7th month after the plan year end and the extended date as 2½ months beyond it.
Compare the recomputed dates to the dates recorded on the calendar row and to the EFAST2 submission timestamp.
Compute days early or late for every sampled filing and record the number, not a pass/fail flag alone.
Where a weekend or federal holiday shifted the date, confirm the shift was applied correctly and consistently.
testing.done: every sampled filing has an independently recomputed due date and a recorded days-early or days-late figure.

testing.step: Verify each Form 5558 was filed on or before the original due date
actions: Pull the Form 5558 confirmation or certified mail receipt for every filing that relied on an extension.
Compare the extension filing date to the plan's original due date — a Form 5558 filed after the original due date gives no extension and makes the return late.
Confirm the plan name, EIN, plan number and plan year end on the Form 5558 match the return it was meant to extend.
Treat any missing, mismatched or late Form 5558 as a late filing regardless of when the return itself went in.
testing.done: every extended filing is supported by a matching Form 5558 evidenced as filed on or before the original due date.

testing.step: Trace SAR distribution to proof of delivery inside the window
actions: For each sampled plan, pull the SAR distribution log with dates, channel, recipient counts and bounce-back handling.
Recompute the deadline as 9 months after plan year end, or 2 months after the extended Form 5500 due date where an extension applied.
Reconcile the recipient count to the participant and beneficiary population from the recordkeeper census and investigate any shortfall over 2%.
For electronic delivery, confirm the safe harbor basis on file — work-related computer access or affirmative consent — for a sample of 10 recipients.
testing.done: each SAR is evidenced as delivered inside its recomputed window to a recipient count reconciled to the census, with the electronic delivery basis verified.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day and 90/120-day disclosure clocks
actions: For the 20 sampled document requests, recompute days from the written request date to the evidenced send date and flag any over 30.
For newly covered participants in the year, recompute days from coverage start to SPD delivery and flag any over 90.
For any newly established plan, confirm SPD delivery within 120 days of the plan becoming subject to ERISA.
For each breach, compute the §502(c)(1) daily penalty exposure at the current per-day maximum and record it as quantified risk, not a note.
testing.done: every sampled disclosure clock is recomputed, each breach has a quantified §502(c)(1) exposure, and the counts are recorded.

testing.step: Test EFAST2 credential custody against the cybersecurity expectations
actions: List every person holding an EFAST2 filing signer credential and compare it to the roles named on the filing calendar.
Confirm no credential is registered to a shared mailbox or a departed employee, and that MFA is enforced on the mailbox behind each credential.
Compare the signer recorded on each sampled filing to the person who actually authenticated, per the credential holder list.
Assess the control set against the EBSA Cybersecurity Program Best Practices in Compliance Assistance Release 2021-01 and list gaps.
testing.done: every filing signer credential is individually held with MFA, matches the signer on the filing, and gaps against CAR 2021-01 are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with plan number, obligation, statutory date, actual date and days late.
Assign a root cause — audit opinion late, carrier Schedule A data late, extension missed, credential lapsed, census error — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for late filings, record the DFVCP eligibility assessment and submission status.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with days late, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date, a DFVCP status and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the filing timeliness test
actions: Compute the on-time rate by obligation type and compare it to the zero-late-statutory-filing threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the acknowledgement IDs and date recomputations behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who holds no EFAST2 credential and prepared no tested filing, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Retirement Committee and the Audit Committee, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an on-time rate, a stated conclusion and a dated committee reporting reference is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the ERISA supplemental schedules attached to the Form 5500 — Schedule of Assets (Held at End of Year), Schedule of Reportable Transactions, Schedule of Delinquent Participant Contributions and Schedule G — and their agreement to the audited financial statements

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 29 CFR 2520.103-10 supplemental schedule content requirements read together with 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) and 29 CFR 2578.1, re-verified against the current-year Form 5500 Instructions for Schedule H lines 4a, 4i and 4j before the schedules are built

In-scope processes.value: Annual supplemental schedule build for every large ERISA plan: end-of-year asset listing with party-in-interest identification, 5% reportable transaction test, delinquent contribution schedule, non-exempt transaction and defaulted loan schedules

In-scope systems.value: Recordkeeper and custodian position and transaction extracts staged in the warehouse for the asset listing and the 5% reportable transaction computation; final schedules attached to the Form 5500 in EFAST2

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Supplemental Schedule Preparation Procedure — asset listing columns and identifiers, party-in-interest flagging rule, 5% threshold denominator, delinquent contribution roll-up, and the schedule-to-financial-statement agreement check

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer with the IQPA engagement partner's confirmation that the schedule formats meet the supplemental schedule reporting requirements; reconfirmed annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — draft schedules to the IQPA within 90 days of plan year end so audit testing can run, final schedules attached to the Form 5500 by July 31 for calendar-year plans or October 15 on a timely Form 5558; interim delinquent contribution schedule refreshed within 30 days of each quarter end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Reminders at plan year end +60 days (custodian extract received), +90 days (draft schedules issued), +150 days (audit comments cleared) and 10 business days before the applicable Form 5500 due date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Asset listing extracts, 5% threshold computation workbook, party-in-interest determination memo and the attached schedule PDFs retained 6 years from the Form 5500 filing date under ERISA §107

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missing supplemental schedule, an asset listed without an identity/cost/value column, an omitted 5% transaction or an understated line 4a amount is logged as an exception with an amended-filing decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off any restated supplemental schedule, any amended Form 5500 filed to add a missing schedule, and the corrective plan for any unreported non-exempt transaction

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every large plan's supplemental schedule set for the plan year, the underlying end-of-year holdings file, the full-year transaction file by security, and the payroll-to-trust contribution timeliness schedule

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any required supplemental schedule absent from the filing is a fail; any asset on the holdings file absent from the asset listing is a fail; any single-security transaction series above 5% of beginning-of-year plan assets omitted from the reportable transaction schedule is a fail; line 4a understated by any amount is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Annual test of the full schedule set at the point the audit file closes, with a quarterly interim test of the delinquent contribution roll-up because that data accrues each pay cycle

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built the asset listing, run the 5% computation or prepared any schedule in the tested year

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual supplemental schedule test workpaper (holdings reconciliation, 5% recomputation, party-in-interest sample, schedule-to-statement tie) in the compliance evidence repository under plan number and plan year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Attached schedule PDFs, the source holdings and transaction extracts, the 5% computation workbook and the party-in-interest memo, producible for an EBSA investigator within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: EBSA questions on a supplemental schedule route to the Controller with Legal Counsel; a missing or defective schedule is cured by amended Form 5500, and any non-exempt transaction surfaced is assessed for VFCP correction and Form 5330 excise tax

checklist.step: Obtain the certified end-of-year holdings extract from the custodian
actions: Request from the custodian and recordkeeper the plan's position file as of the last day of the plan year with CUSIP or other identifier, security description, share or par quantity, cost, and current value for every holding.
Load the file into the warehouse staging table keyed on plan number, and confirm the row count and total market value against the certified trust statement.
Request the look-through detail for any common collective trust, pooled separate account or master trust so the plan's participation is reportable on Schedule D.
Reject any extract lacking cost data for non-participant-directed assets — cost is a required column on the asset listing.
Hand the accepted extract to the Senior Accountant with the reconciliation to net assets attached.
checklist.done: the holdings extract is loaded, reconciled to certified trust net assets, and carries identifier, description, quantity, cost and value on every row.

checklist.step: Build the Schedule of Assets (Held at End of Year)
actions: Build the schedule in the 29 CFR 2520.103-10 column order: (a) party-in-interest indicator, (b) identity of issue/borrower/lessor/similar party, (c) description including maturity date, rate of interest, collateral, par or maturity value, (d) cost, (e) current value.
Populate column (c) fully for participant loans — interest rate range and maturity dates — and for any debt instrument.
Omit cost in column (d) only where the asset is participant-directed, and state that basis in the schedule footnote.
Foot the current value column and agree the total to the Statement of Net Assets investments line to the dollar.
Label the schedule with plan name, EIN, plan number and plan year end as the audit report will reference it.
checklist.done: the asset listing carries all five required columns, is footed, and its total agrees to the investments line in the audited statements.

checklist.step: Identify and flag every party-in-interest holding
actions: Build the party-in-interest list under ERISA §3(14): the sponsor and affiliates, plan fiduciaries, the trustee, recordkeeper, investment managers, service providers, unions representing covered employees, and 50%-or-more owners.
Match the asset listing issuers and counterparties against that list on name and, where available, LEI or tax ID.
Mark column (a) with an asterisk on every matched row — participant loans and employer securities always qualify.

Write a determination memo naming each flagged party, the relationship that makes it a party in interest, and the exemption relied on (e.g. §408(b)(1) participant loans, §408(b)(2) reasonable service arrangements).
Circulate the memo to Legal Counsel for confirmation before the schedule is finalised.
checklist.done: every party-in-interest row is asterisked and covered by a counsel-confirmed determination memo naming the relationship and the exemption.

checklist.step: Run the 5% reportable transaction computation
actions: Set the denominator: plan current value of assets at the beginning of the plan year, taken from the prior-year Statement of Net Assets.
Pull the full-year transaction file and aggregate purchases and sales separately by security identifier, treating a series of transactions in the same security as one series.
Compute each aggregate against 5% of the beginning-of-year denominator and list every series that exceeds it.
Exclude transactions in participant-directed accounts from the reportable transaction schedule and state that exclusion basis in the workbook.
Save the computation workbook with the denominator, the threshold value and the full ranked list, not only the exceedances.
checklist.done: the 5% threshold is computed from a documented beginning-of-year denominator and every exceeding series is identified from the ranked full list.

checklist.step: Build the Schedule of Reportable Transactions
actions: For each reportable series list: identity of party involved, description of asset including par or maturity value, purchase price, selling price, lease rental, expenses incurred with the transaction, cost of asset, current value of asset on the transaction date, and net gain or loss.
Split single transactions from series of transactions on separate schedule sections as the instructions require.
Agree the net gain or loss column to the realized gain/loss recognised in the Statement of Changes.
Set Schedule H line 4j to Yes where any reportable transaction exists and attach this schedule.
Where no series exceeds the threshold, retain the computation workbook as the evidence that the schedule is genuinely not required.
checklist.done: each reportable series is presented with all nine required data elements and its net gain/loss agrees to the audited statements.

checklist.step: Build the Schedule of Delinquent Participant Contributions
actions: Take the payroll-to-trust timeliness schedule from the Payroll Specialist and isolate every cycle where deferrals or loan repayments reached the trust later than the earliest reasonably segregable date.
Present, per plan year, the total that was late, whether it was fully corrected, and whether it is included in the VFCP filing.
Reconcile the total to Schedule H line 4a and confirm the Form 5500 answer is Yes.
Add the lost earnings deposited and the deposit date so a reader can see the correction, not only the failure.
Where amounts remain uncorrected at the filing date, say so on the schedule rather than presenting the failure as closed.
checklist.done: the delinquent contribution schedule reconciles to Schedule H line 4a and shows the corrected amount, lost earnings and deposit dates.

checklist.step: Build Schedule G for defaulted loans, leases and non-exempt transactions
actions: Part I: list every loan or fixed income obligation in default or classified as uncollectible with the obligor, original amount, amount overdue for principal and interest, and the detailed description.
Part II: list any lease in default or uncollectible with the same level of detail.
Part III: list every non-exempt transaction with a party in interest, with the relationship, description, purchase and selling price, cost, current value and net gain or loss.
Pull defaulted participant loan data from the recordkeeper's deemed distribution report and reconcile it to Schedule H line 2g.
Refer every Part III entry to Legal Counsel for a prohibited transaction assessment before the filing goes out.
checklist.done: Schedule G Parts I-III are complete, defaulted loans reconcile to the deemed distribution report, and every Part III entry has a counsel assessment.

checklist.step: Build Schedule C service provider and indirect compensation disclosure
actions: Collect the 29 CFR 2550.408b-2 fee disclosures from every covered service provider — recordkeeper, investment managers, custodian, auditor, consultant, third-party administrator.
List every service provider receiving $5,000 or more in direct or indirect compensation with its EIN, service codes and compensation amount.

Identify indirect compensation (revenue sharing, 12b-1 fees, sub-transfer agency fees) and apply the eligible indirect compensation alternative reporting option only where its written-disclosure conditions are met.
List any service provider that failed or refused to supply the required information in the Part II section reserved for it.
Reconcile total fees on Schedule C to administrative expenses on Schedule H line 2i.
checklist.done: every provider at or above $5,000 is listed with service codes and compensation, indirect compensation is treated and reconciled to line 2i.

checklist.step: Build Schedule A from carrier data and Schedule D from pooled arrangements
actions: Request the ERISA §103(a)(2) annual report from each insurance carrier providing benefits or holding plan assets — persons receiving commissions, fees paid, premiums, and the contract's experience.
Complete Schedule A per contract with the carrier name, NAIC code, contract number, policy year dates and the commission and fee detail by recipient.

Complete Schedule D listing every common collective trust, pooled separate account, master trust investment account or 103-12 IE the plan participated in, with the DFE name, EIN, plan number and dollar value of interest at year end.
Reconcile each Schedule D value to the corresponding line on the asset listing.
Escalate to the Regulatory Reporting Manager any carrier that has not supplied its report 60 days before the due date.
checklist.done: a Schedule A exists per insurance contract with carrier-supplied commission detail, and every Schedule D interest ties to the asset listing.

checklist.step: Agree the supplemental schedules to the audited financial statements
actions: Tie the asset listing total to the investments line, the reportable transaction gains to realized gains, the delinquent contributions to line 4a and Schedule C fees to line 2i.
Record each tie in the schedule tie-out tab with the statement page reference so a reader can retrace it.
Resolve every difference before issuing the schedules to the IQPA — the auditor reports on these schedules in relation to the financial statements as a whole.
Sign the tie-out tab as reviewer with name and date.
checklist.done: every supplemental schedule total ties to a named line in the audited statements with the tie evidenced and signed.

checklist.step: Clear the IQPA's supplemental schedule comments
actions: Log each auditor comment on the schedules — missing column, wrong identifier, unflagged party in interest, misapplied threshold — with an owner.
Correct the schedule at source in the build workbook rather than editing the output PDF, then reissue the schedule with a version number.
Reconfirm the tie-out after every correction so a fix on one schedule does not break another.
Obtain written auditor agreement that the schedules are ready for attachment before the filing is signed.
checklist.done: every auditor comment is closed with a versioned corrected schedule and written auditor agreement to attach.

checklist.step: Attach the schedule set to the Form 5500 and set the driver answers
actions: In EFAST2 IFILE attach the supplemental schedules as part of the accountant's report attachment, in the order the audit report references them.
Set the Schedule H driver answers that require a schedule: line 4a delinquent contributions, line 4b-4h loans/leases/non-exempt transactions driving Schedule G, line 4j reportable transactions.
Confirm every Yes answer has a corresponding attached schedule and every attached schedule has a Yes answer behind it.
Run the EFAST2 validation and clear any attachment-related error before submission.
checklist.done: every Yes driver answer on Schedule H has its matching attached schedule and validation returns no attachment errors.

checklist.step: Refresh the delinquent contribution schedule each quarter
actions: Within 30 days of each quarter end, rerun the deferral withholding to trust deposit comparison for that quarter's payroll cycles.
Add any newly identified late cycle to the running delinquent contribution schedule with the amount and days late.
Compute lost earnings on the new items through the DOL VFCP Online Calculator and hand the correction instruction to the Benefits Administrator.
Report the quarter's count and dollar value of late cycles to the Controller so the year-end line 4a figure is never a surprise.
checklist.done: the delinquent contribution schedule is refreshed within 30 days of each quarter end with lost earnings computed on every new item.

checklist.step: Assess unreported non-exempt transactions for correction and excise tax
actions: Review every Schedule G Part III entry and every delinquent contribution amount against the ERISA §406 prohibited transaction rules and the §408 exemptions.
Where a prohibited transaction is confirmed, decide with the Head of Compliance whether to correct under VFCP and whether the PTE 2002-51 excise tax relief conditions are met.
Where relief is unavailable, instruct the Tax Manager to file Form 5330 and pay the excise tax on the amount involved.
Record the analysis, the decision and the correction date in the plan legal file and on the exception log.
checklist.done: every non-exempt transaction has a documented §406/§408 analysis, a correction decision and either a VFCP filing or a Form 5330.

checklist.step: Archive the schedule build evidence under ERISA retention
actions: File the holdings extract, transaction file, 5% computation workbook, party-in-interest memo, tie-out tab and the final attached schedule PDFs under plan number and plan year.
Apply the 6-year-from-filing ERISA §107 retention label to the whole package.
Confirm the package is searchable by plan number, plan year and security identifier so an EBSA request can be answered from the index.
Grant read access to the Internal Auditor and the IQPA for the following year's cycle.
checklist.done: the schedule build package is archived with a 6-year retention label and is searchable by plan number, plan year and security identifier.

testing.step: Build the population of required supplemental schedules
actions: List every large plan for the plan year and, for each, derive which supplemental schedules the Schedule H answers require.
Pull the accepted Form 5500 attachments from EFAST2 by acknowledgement ID and inventory the schedules actually attached.
Reconcile required to attached and list every gap in either direction — a schedule attached with no Yes answer is as much a defect as the reverse.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and counts.
testing.done: required and attached supplemental schedules are reconciled per plan with every gap listed, and the population is signed.

testing.step: Reconcile the asset listing to the custodian holdings file
actions: Obtain the custodian end-of-year position file directly from the custodian portal, not from the preparer's copy.
Match it to the filed asset listing on security identifier and compare quantity, cost and current value on every row.
List every holding present in the custodian file and absent from the listing, and every value difference over $1,000.
Foot the filed listing independently and compare to the investments line in the audited Statement of Net Assets.
testing.done: the filed asset listing reconciles row-for-row to the custodian file and its independently computed total agrees to the audited statements.

testing.step: Draw and document the schedule testing sample
actions: Take 100% of plans with any Schedule G entry, any line 4a amount, or any party-in-interest flag.
Take a seeded random sample of 25 asset listing rows and 100% of reportable transaction series.
Take a seeded random sample of 10 Schedule C service providers.
Record the seed, population sizes, selection date and stratification rationale so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all Schedule G, line 4a and reportable transaction items in full.

testing.step: Recompute the 5% reportable transaction threshold independently
actions: Take the beginning-of-year plan asset value from the prior-year filed Schedule H, not from the preparer's workbook, and compute 5% of it.
Aggregate the custodian transaction file independently by security identifier for purchases and for sales.
Compare your exceedance list to the filed schedule and treat any omitted series as a fail regardless of dollar size.
Confirm the participant-directed exclusion was applied to genuinely participant-directed accounts only, by sampling five excluded securities.
testing.done: the 5% threshold and the exceedance list are independently recomputed and reconcile to the filed schedule with no omissions.

testing.step: Re-perform the party-in-interest identification on the sample
actions: Build your own ERISA §3(14) party list from the plan document, service agreements and the sponsor's affiliate register.
Match the 25 sampled asset listing rows against it independently and compare to the filed column (a) flags.
For each flagged row, confirm the determination memo names the relationship and the exemption relied on.
Treat an unflagged party-in-interest holding as an exception and assess whether it should also have appeared on Schedule G Part III.
testing.done: party-in-interest flags on the sample are independently re-derived and every flag is supported by a named relationship and exemption.

testing.step: Recompute the delinquent contribution amount reported on line 4a
actions: Pull all payroll cycles for the plan year and independently compute days from deferral withholding to trust posting.
Sum the amounts on every cycle exceeding the earliest reasonably segregable date and compare to the filed schedule and Schedule H line 4a.
Recompute lost earnings on 5 late cycles using the DOL VFCP Online Calculator and compare to the amounts actually deposited.
Treat any understatement of line 4a, however small, as a fail against the stated threshold.
testing.done: the line 4a amount and lost earnings are independently recomputed and agree to the filed schedule with no understatement.

testing.step: Trace Schedule C fees and Schedule A carrier data to source disclosures
actions: For the 10 sampled service providers, open the 29 CFR 2550.408b-2 fee disclosure and compare the compensation reported on Schedule C to it.
Confirm indirect compensation is either reported in full or covered by a properly evidenced eligible indirect compensation alternative.
For each insurance contract, compare Schedule A commission and fee detail to the carrier's ERISA §103(a)(2) report and confirm the NAIC code and contract number.
Reconcile total Schedule C fees to Schedule H line 2i and list any difference.
testing.done: sampled Schedule C amounts trace to 408b-2 disclosures, Schedule A ties to carrier reports, and total fees reconcile to line 2i.

testing.step: Verify Schedule G completeness against defaulted loan and transaction data
actions: Pull the recordkeeper deemed distribution and loan default report for the plan year.
Compare it to Schedule G Part I and to Schedule H line 2g and list any default not shown on the schedule.
Compare the Part III non-exempt transaction list to the party-in-interest matching results from the earlier step.
Confirm each Part III entry carries a dated Legal Counsel prohibited transaction assessment and a correction decision.
testing.done: every loan default and non-exempt transaction is present on Schedule G, reconciled to line 2g, with a dated counsel assessment on each Part III entry.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with plan number, schedule affected, the omitted or misstated item and its dollar value.
Assign a root cause — incomplete custodian extract, wrong 5% denominator, party list not refreshed, payroll cut-off — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the filing itself is defective, record the amended Form 5500 decision and target date.
Carry every open exception into the next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a dollar value, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an amended-filing decision where relevant.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the supplemental schedule test
actions: Compute the exception rate by schedule type against the stated zero-omission thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the recomputation workpapers behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who built no schedule and ran no 5% computation in the tested year, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Retirement Committee and the Audit Committee, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an exception rate by schedule type, a stated conclusion and a dated committee reporting reference is filed.
