checklist.step: Trigger the audit requirement from the first-day participant count
actions: Within 30 days of the plan year starting, obtain the recordkeeper census as of the first day of the plan year and count participants with account balances.
Apply the 100-participant threshold and the 80-120 rule, and record the resulting filer status against each plan.
Send the Controller the list of plans crossing into large-plan status this year — those need an audit for the first time and a longer lead time.
Flag any plan expected to cross the threshold next year so the recordkeeper data quality work starts a year early.
checklist.done: the Controller holds a dated list of plans requiring an ERISA §103(a)(3)(A) audit this year, including first-time large plans.

checklist.step: Select the IQPA and confirm independence and licensure
actions: Shortlist firms with a demonstrated employee benefit plan practice, ideally AICPA Employee Benefit Plan Audit Quality Center members, and request their most recent peer review report.
Confirm the engagement partner and firm hold current CPA licences in the state and that the firm is independent of the plan and the sponsor under ERISA §103(a)(3)(A) and AICPA independence rules.
Confirm no partner or professional on the engagement holds an interest in the sponsor or serves in a plan fiduciary or recordkeeping capacity.
Obtain a written independence confirmation naming the plan and the plan year.
Take the appointment and the fee to the Audit Committee for approval and record the resolution.
checklist.done: an independent, peer-reviewed IQPA is appointed with a written independence confirmation and a recorded Audit Committee approval.

checklist.step: Execute the engagement letter with the scope election stated
actions: Review the draft engagement letter for the plan name, EIN, plan number, plan year, scope, fee and the auditor's and management's responsibilities.
State the audit scope election explicitly: a full-scope audit, or an ERISA §103(a)(3)(C) audit with the certification basis named.
Confirm the letter includes the management acknowledgements AU-C 703 requires — maintaining the plan instrument, administering the plan, and determining that a §103(a)(3)(C) audit is permissible.
Route for signature to the Plan Administrator representative and the engagement partner and store the executed letter in the plan file.
Sign the letter within 60 days of plan year end so fieldwork scheduling is not the constraint.
checklist.done: a signed engagement letter naming the plan, plan year, scope election and the AU-C 703 acknowledgements is in the plan file within 60 days of year end.

checklist.step: Validate the §103(a)(3)(C) certification before relying on it
actions: Obtain the certification from the bank, similar institution or insurance carrier holding the assets and confirm it is signed by an authorised officer.
Confirm the certification covers both the completeness and the accuracy of the investment information — a certification of accuracy alone does not support the election.
Confirm the certifying institution is regulated, supervised and subject to periodic examination by a state or federal agency.
Identify any asset not covered by the certification — self-directed brokerage, real estate, employer securities, alternatives — and tell the auditor to scope it into full testing.
File the certification with the engagement letter as the support for the Schedule H line 3d(2) coding.
checklist.done: a signed certification covering completeness and accuracy from a qualifying institution is on file, with non-certified assets identified for full testing.

checklist.step: Deliver the prepared-by-client package on the agreed standard
actions: Load the auditor's PBC list into the audit workspace with an owner and due date on every line and a single point of contact per workstream.
Deliver the governing documents: plan document and all amendments, adoption agreement, IRS determination or opinion letter, trust agreement, service agreements and the ERISA fidelity bond.
Deliver the financial data: certified trust statement, trial balance, Schedule H tie-out, payroll registers, contribution timeliness schedule and the distribution register.
Deliver the participant data: full-year census with hire, termination, eligibility, compensation, deferral election and vesting service fields.
Close the whole list within 90 days of plan year end and escalate any item open more than five business days to the Controller.
checklist.done: 100% of PBC items are delivered within 90 days of plan year end with no item open beyond five business days unescalated.

checklist.step: Supply the SOC 1 reports and evidence the user entity controls
actions: Obtain the SOC 1 Type 2 report from the recordkeeper, the trustee/custodian and any payroll provider whose processing affects the plan.
Confirm each report's period covers the whole plan year; where it does not, obtain a bridge letter covering the gap and give both to the auditor.

Extract the complementary user entity controls from each report and evidence that the sponsor actually performs them — participant data reviews, transaction report reconciliations, access administration.
List every exception noted in the service auditor's testing and assess its effect on the plan with the Controller.
Upload the reports, bridge letters and the user entity control evidence to the audit workspace.
checklist.done: SOC 1 Type 2 coverage exists for the full plan year for every relevant provider, with user entity controls evidenced and exceptions assessed.

checklist.step: Support compliance testing on participant data and plan operations
actions: Give the auditor the sample-support pack for participant testing: enrolment forms, deferral election changes, distribution requests, loan applications and beneficiary designations.
Reconcile the definition of compensation used for deferrals and match to the plan document definition and explain any exclusion applied.
Provide the eligibility computation for the auditor's sample of new entrants and the vesting service computation for terminated participants who took distributions.
Provide the ADP/ACP nondiscrimination test results, the top-heavy determination and evidence of any corrective distribution made inside its correction window.
Respond to auditor sample requests within three business days so fieldwork does not stall.
checklist.done: every participant sample request is answered within three business days with source documents, and compensation, eligibility and vesting computations are supplied.

checklist.step: Run the fieldwork exit meeting and log every finding
actions: Hold the exit meeting with the engagement partner, the Compensation & Benefits Manager and the Retirement Operations Administrator within 120 days of plan year end.
Log every proposed adjustment, uncorrected misstatement, internal control deficiency and operational failure on the findings log with an owner and a due date.
Classify each control finding as a deficiency, significant deficiency or material weakness and record the auditor's basis for the classification.
Agree in writing which findings will be corrected before the opinion and which will be reported to those charged with governance.
Circulate the findings log to the Audit Committee chair the same week.
checklist.done: a findings log exists with a classification, owner and due date on every item, agreed in writing with the engagement partner.

checklist.step: Correct operational failures under EPCRS before the opinion is issued
actions: For each operational failure identified — missed deferral opportunity, wrong compensation definition, late deposits, improper exclusion of eligible employees — select the correction method from the current EPCRS revenue procedure.
Compute the corrective contribution, the missed match and the earnings adjustment, and process the deposit through the recordkeeper.
Decide with Legal Counsel whether self-correction is available or a Voluntary Correction Program submission with Form 8950 is required.
Notify affected participants where the correction changes their account and retain the notice.
Give the auditor the correction memo, the calculation and the deposit confirmation before the opinion date.
checklist.done: every operational failure has a named EPCRS correction method, a computed and deposited correction, and evidence supplied to the auditor.

checklist.step: Sign the management representation letter
actions: Read the representation letter in full — it covers completeness of plan records, disclosure of all plan amendments, party-in-interest and non-exempt transactions, subsequent events and the §103(a)(3)(C) permissibility acknowledgement.
Confirm with the Controller and the Compensation & Benefits Manager that every representation is factually supportable before signing.
Refuse to sign any representation not supported by evidence and resolve the underlying fact first.
Date the letter no earlier than the audit report date and return the signed original to the engagement partner.
File the executed letter in the plan audit file.
checklist.done: a signed representation letter dated no earlier than the audit report date is with the auditor and filed in the plan audit file.

checklist.step: Receive the opinion, classify it and code Schedule H line 3
actions: Receive the manually signed audit report on firm letterhead, dated, naming the plan, the plan year and the city and state of the issuing office.
Classify the opinion as unmodified, qualified, adverse or disclaimer, and separately record whether it is an ERISA §103(a)(3)(C) report.
Complete the Schedule H line 3 coding worksheet with the opinion type, the accountant's name, EIN and address.
Where the opinion is modified, brief the CFO, the Retirement Committee and the Audit Committee on the cause and the remediation before filing.
Confirm the opinion is in hand at least 15 business days before the Form 5500 due date, and escalate immediately if not.
checklist.done: a signed, dated opinion is in hand with its type classified onto the Schedule H line 3 worksheet at least 15 business days before the due date.

checklist.step: Attach the audited statements and opinion to the Form 5500
actions: In EFAST2 IFILE open the plan's Schedule H and load the accountant's opinion attachment slot.
Attach the signed opinion, the audited statements, the notes and the supplemental schedules as a single searchable PDF.
Complete Schedule H lines 3a-3d from the coding worksheet and confirm line 3d(2) is used only where a §103(a)(3)(C) audit applies.
Run validation and confirm no missing-attachment error remains — a large-plan filing without the auditor's report is incomplete and will be rejected.
Record the acknowledgement ID and attachment file name against the plan row in the filing calendar.
checklist.done: the signed opinion and audited statements are attached to Schedule H, line 3 coding matches the opinion, and validation returns no attachment error.

checklist.step: Report the audit outcome to the Audit and Retirement Committees
actions: Present per plan: the opinion type, the number and classification of control findings, uncorrected misstatements, and any EPCRS correction made.
Present the auditor's governance communication letter and management's written response to each point.
Record the committee's acceptance and any directed action with an owner and a due date in the minutes.
Table the IQPA fee and reappointment decision for the following year at the same meeting.
checklist.done: committee minutes record the opinion type, findings, management responses and the reappointment decision for every plan.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate any plan that reached the deadline without an opinion
actions: Fifteen business days before the due date, list any large plan without a signed opinion and escalate to the CFO and the Audit Committee chair the same day.
Decide in writing between filing Form 5558 for the remaining extension, or accepting a late filing with a DFVCP cure — never file a large-plan return with no opinion attached to buy time.
Where the return was already filed incomplete, prepare the amended Form 5500 with the opinion attached and file it as soon as the opinion is signed.
Record the root cause — late census, unresponsive recordkeeper, unresolved reconciliation, engagement signed late — and the process fix with an owner.
checklist.done: every plan short of an opinion at the deadline has a written filing decision, an amendment plan where needed, and a root-cause fix with an owner.

checklist.step: Archive the audit file under ERISA retention
actions: File the engagement letter, independence confirmation, peer review report, PBC delivery log, SOC 1 reports and bridge letters, findings log, EPCRS correction memos, representation letter and the signed opinion under plan number and plan year.
Apply the 6-year-from-filing ERISA §107 retention label to the package.
Confirm the index makes the file retrievable by EIN, plan number, plan year and audit firm name.
Grant read access to the Internal Auditor and the succeeding year's engagement team.
checklist.done: the complete audit file is archived with a 6-year retention label and is retrievable by EIN, plan number, plan year and audit firm.

testing.step: Build the population of plans requiring an ERISA audit
actions: Extract every ERISA plan from the plan inventory with EIN, plan number, plan year end and first-day participant count.
Independently derive large-plan status from the recordkeeper census rather than accepting the recorded filer status.
Add plans acquired, merged or terminated in the year so short-plan-year audits enter the population.
Reconcile to the prior-year EFAST2 filings by EIN and sign the population as complete with counts and extract date.
testing.done: the audit-required population is independently derived from census data, reconciled to prior-year filings and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every audit-required plan to a signed engagement and an opinion
actions: Match each population row to a signed engagement letter on plan number plus plan year.
Match each row to a signed audit report and compare the report date to the Form 5500 submission date.
List any plan with no engagement letter, no opinion, or an opinion dated after the filing date as an automatic exception.
Capture the engagement letter and opinion first pages into the workpaper as evidence of the match.
testing.done: every audit-required plan is matched to a signed engagement letter and an opinion dated on or before the filing, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the audit oversight sample
actions: Take 100% of large plans, 100% of first-time large plans and 100% of plans with a modified opinion.
Take a seeded random sample of 5 plans classified as small to confirm the classification held.
Within each sampled plan select the independence confirmation, the certification (where §103(a)(3)(C) applies), the representation letter and the findings log for testing.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rationale in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers 100% of large, first-time large and modified-opinion plans and is reproducible from a recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-verify IQPA independence and licensure
actions: Confirm the engagement partner and the firm hold active CPA licences by checking the relevant state board of accountancy register on the audit report date.
Read the written independence confirmation and confirm it names the specific plan and plan year.
Cross-check the firm and its partners against the sponsor's vendor master and fiduciary register for any non-audit relationship that would impair independence.
Confirm a peer review report exists and note any peer review rating other than pass.
testing.done: licensure is verified against the state board register, independence is confirmed in writing per plan and year, and peer review status is recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the §103(a)(3)(C) permissibility assessment
actions: For each sampled plan taking a §103(a)(3)(C) audit, read the certification and independently confirm it addresses both completeness and accuracy.
Confirm the certifying institution qualifies — a bank, similar institution or insurance carrier regulated, supervised and subject to periodic examination.
Confirm the management acknowledgement of permissibility appears in the engagement letter and the representation letter.
Identify any asset class excluded from certification and confirm the auditor performed full testing on it; an unsupported election is a fail.
testing.done: each scope election is independently confirmed against a qualifying certification and both management acknowledgements, with non-certified assets tested.

testing.step: Verify the opinion attachment and the Schedule H line 3 coding
actions: Retrieve the accepted Form 5500 from EFAST2 by acknowledgement ID for each sampled plan.
Open the accountant's opinion attachment and confirm it is manually signed, dated, on firm letterhead and names the plan and plan year.
Compare the opinion type in the attachment to Schedule H line 3a and the firm name, EIN and address to line 3c.
Confirm line 3d(2) is used only where a §103(a)(3)(C) audit is genuinely in place and log any mismatch as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled filing carries a signed opinion whose type and firm details agree with Schedule H line 3, with mismatches logged.

testing.step: Recompute the audit timeline against the milestone deadlines
actions: For each sampled plan compute days from plan year end to engagement letter signature, PBC completion, fieldwork exit and opinion date.
Compare each to the 60/90/120/150-day milestones and to the 15-business-day pre-filing buffer.
Compute the buffer actually achieved between the opinion date and the Form 5500 submission and flag any plan under 15 business days.
Correlate late milestones with the exceptions logged during the year to test whether the escalation actually fired.
testing.done: every sampled plan has recomputed milestone day counts, an achieved pre-filing buffer figure, and any missed escalation is identified.

testing.step: Test the findings log and the EPCRS corrections through to completion
actions: Pull the auditor's governance communication letter and compare every point raised to the internal findings log — a point raised by the auditor and absent from the log is a control failure.
For each operational failure, trace the EPCRS correction method, the computation, the deposit confirmation and the participant notice.
Confirm self-correction eligibility was assessed and that a VCP submission was made where self-correction was unavailable.
Confirm every material weakness and significant deficiency has an owner, a due date and evidence of remediation or an accepted extension.
testing.done: every auditor-raised point appears on the findings log, and every operational failure traces to a computed, deposited and notified EPCRS correction.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with plan number, plan year, the failure (no engagement, late opinion, independence gap, unsupported scope election, unattached opinion) and its filing consequence.
Assign a root cause — participant count derived late, engagement signed late, recordkeeper data delays, certification not obtained — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the filing is defective, record the amended Form 5500 decision and target filing date.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with a filing consequence, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an amendment decision where relevant.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the plan audit oversight test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold on missing or late opinions.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the engagement, independence and attachment evidence behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who managed no IQPA relationship and signed no representation letter, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any missing-audit findings to the Audit Committee and the Retirement Committee, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an exception rate, a stated conclusion and a dated committee reporting reference is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the continuously maintained ERISA obligation calendar covering Form 5500 series, participant disclosures and the 29 CFR 2560.503-1 claims and appeals clocks, with the evidence of timeliness behind every entry

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 29 CFR 2560.503-1(b) reasonable claims procedure requirements, with the notification timeframes in 2560.503-1(f) and appeal timeframes in 2560.503-1(i), re-verified against eCFR on each calendar review and whenever EBSA issues a disaster-relief extension

In-scope processes.value: Continuous calendar maintenance for every ERISA plan: annual filings, participant disclosure windows, and the per-claim clocks for group health, disability, pension and life claims — initial determinations, extensions, appeals and external review

In-scope systems.value: Claim and appeal cases carry the received date, statutory due date and clock status; the annual filing and disclosure obligations are held on the same calendar with owner, due date and evidence link

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Obligation Calendar and Claims Timeliness Procedure — calendar entry standard (obligation, citation, owner, due date, evidence artifact), clock-start rules, tolling for incomplete claims, extension notice rules, and the SPD description of the claims procedure

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Corporate Secretary as Plan Administrator; reviewed quarterly and re-approved on any change to plan claims procedures or to the DOL claims regulation

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous — group health post-service claims decided within 30 days (one 15-day extension), pre-service within 15 days, urgent care within 72 hours; disability claims within 45 days with up to two 30-day extensions; appeals within 60 days (group health) or 45 days (pension/disability); documents furnished on request within 30 days; plus every annual Form 5500 and disclosure date on the same calendar

Deadline reminders configured.value: Case-level alerts at 50% and 80% of each claim clock and a breach alert at expiry; calendar-level alerts at 30, 10 and 3 business days before every annual filing and disclosure date; a daily aged-case report to the Complaints Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Claim and appeal case records with received dates, determination letters, extension notices and delivery proof, plus filing acknowledgements, retained 6 years from the filing or determination date under ERISA §107 and longer where the benefit entitlement remains live under §209

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any claim or appeal decided after its regulatory clock, any extension taken without a timely written notice, and any calendar entry closed without evidence is logged as an exception with the deemed-exhaustion consequence recorded

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every breached claims clock, the remediation of any calendar entry closed without evidence, and the response where a claimant is deemed to have exhausted administrative remedies under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l)

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every calendar obligation with a due date in the test period, plus every benefit claim and appeal decided in the period across group health, disability, pension and life, with its received date and determination date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on regulatory claim clocks — one determination outside 30/15/72-hour or 45-day limits without a valid written extension notice is a fail; any calendar entry marked complete with no evidence artifact attached is a fail; claim clock accuracy must be 100% on the tested sample

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Monthly test of the claims and appeals clocks because the obligation runs continuously, plus a quarterly test of calendar completeness against the statutory obligation inventory

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own any calendar entry and must not have adjudicated or approved any sampled claim or appeal

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly claims timeliness workpaper and quarterly calendar completeness workpaper (obligation inventory, case extract, clock recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The obligation calendar export with evidence links, the claims procedure as described in the SPD, and per-claim files with received date, determination letter and delivery proof — producible for an EBSA benefits advisor enquiry or a §502(a)(1)(B) suit within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: EBSA Benefits Advisor enquiries and participant complaints route to the Complaints Manager with Legal Counsel; where a clock was missed, the claim is treated as deemed exhausted under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) and the position is cleared with Legal Counsel before any response is sent

checklist.step: Build the statutory obligation inventory the calendar must cover
actions: List every ERISA obligation the sponsor carries: Form 5500 series and Form 8955-SSA, PBGC premiums, SAR, SPD and SMM delivery, 404a-5 participant fee disclosure, 408b-2 provider disclosure receipt, blackout notices, and the 2560.503-1 claim and appeal clocks.
For each, record the citation, the triggering event, the day count, the responsible role and the evidence artifact that proves completion.
Cross-check the list against the plan document and SPD for any plan-specific commitment shorter than the regulatory minimum — the plan's own promise governs where it is stricter.
Have Legal Counsel confirm the citation and day count on every row before the inventory is loaded.
Load the confirmed inventory into the GRC obligation register as the source the calendar is generated from.
checklist.done: the obligation register holds every ERISA obligation with citation, trigger, day count, owner and named evidence artifact, confirmed by counsel.

checklist.step: Generate the calendar entries and assign a named owner to each
actions: Generate a dated calendar entry from every register row for every plan, deriving the date from the plan year end or the triggering event.
Assign a named individual owner and a named backup to each entry — never a team mailbox.
Set the required evidence artifact on the entry so it cannot be closed without an attachment.
Configure reminders at 30, 10 and 3 business days before each date, escalating to the Regulatory Reporting Manager at 3 days.
Publish the calendar to the Retirement Committee and confirm no plan is missing from it.
checklist.done: every register row has a dated calendar entry per plan with a named owner, backup, required evidence artifact and configured reminders.

checklist.step: Configure the claim clocks in the case management workflow
actions: Create a case type per claim category with the regulatory clock built in: urgent care 72 hours, pre-service 15 days, post-service 30 days, disability 45 days, pension 90 days.
Configure the clock to start on the date the claim is received at the address designated in the SPD, not the date it reaches the adjudicator's queue.

Build the extension path so an extension can only be applied where a written notice is generated before the original period expires, stating the special circumstances and the date a decision is expected.
Build the tolling rule for incomplete claims: the clock tolls from the date the request for further information is sent until the claimant responds, with a minimum 45 days given to respond.
Test the configuration with the QA Analyst on ten scenario cases per category before it goes live.
checklist.done: each claim category has a configured clock, an extension gate requiring a prior written notice, and a tested tolling rule.

checklist.step: Describe the claims procedure accurately in the SPD
actions: Compare the SPD claims section to the configured procedure: where to file, the decision timeframes, the appeal deadline, the review process and the right to bring a §502(a) civil action.
Confirm the SPD states the claimant's right to receive, free of charge, all documents relevant to the claim on request.
Confirm the SPD does not impose any procedure that unduly inhibits a claim — no filing fee, no more than two levels of mandatory appeal.
Issue a Summary of Material Modifications where the procedure changed, within 210 days after the plan year in which the change was adopted.
Sign off the SPD claims section with a date so the calendar entry can close against it.
checklist.done: the SPD claims section matches the configured procedure, states the §502(a) right, and any change is covered by a timely SMM.

checklist.step: Log every claim on receipt with its clock start date
actions: Open a case on the day the claim is received at the designated filing address and record the received date, the channel and the claim category.
Confirm the claim meets the plan's definition of a filed claim; where it does not, send the deficiency notice inside the timeframe rather than leaving the case unopened.
Attach the claim form and every submitted document to the case at intake.
Confirm the system-computed statutory due date on screen and correct the category if the date looks wrong for the claim type.
Route the case to the adjudication queue the same business day.
checklist.done: every claim has a case opened on its received date with the correct category, a system-computed due date and the documents attached.

checklist.step: Work the daily aged-case report before any clock expires
actions: Run the aged-case report each morning showing every open claim and appeal with days elapsed, days remaining and the owner.
Work the 80%-of-clock band first and confirm with each owner what is outstanding and whether an extension notice is needed.
Escalate any case with under 20% of its clock remaining to the Claims Director / Manager the same day.
Record on the case the reason for any case reaching the escalation band so the root cause is visible later.
Report the count of cases in each band to the Head of Compliance weekly.
checklist.done: the aged-case report is worked daily with every case under 20% of clock remaining escalated and its cause recorded.

checklist.step: Issue extension notices before the original period expires
actions: Where a decision cannot be made in the initial period, generate the extension notice before the original period expires — a notice issued afterwards does not extend anything.
State in the notice the special circumstances requiring the extension and the date by which a decision will be rendered.
Where the extension is caused by missing information, specify the information needed and give the claimant at least 45 days to supply it, and record the tolling start.
Send the notice through the channel evidenced on the case and attach the delivery proof.
Update the case due date only from the generated notice, never by manual override.
checklist.done: every extension is supported by a notice issued before the original period expired, stating the circumstances and the new decision date, with delivery proof attached.

checklist.step: Issue adverse benefit determinations with the required content
actions: Draft the determination letter with the specific reason for the denial, reference to the specific plan provisions relied on, a description of any additional material needed and why, and a description of the appeal procedure and time limits.
Include the statement of the claimant's right to bring a civil action under ERISA §502(a) following an adverse determination on appeal.

Where an internal rule, guideline or protocol was relied on, either state it or state that it is available free on request; where the denial is based on medical necessity or experimental treatment, include the scientific or clinical judgement explanation.
Send the letter inside the clock and attach it plus delivery proof to the case.
Close the case only when the letter and delivery proof are both attached.
checklist.done: each adverse determination is issued inside the clock with reasons, plan provisions, appeal rights, §502(a) notice and delivery proof on the case.

checklist.step: Run the appeal within its own clock and with a fresh reviewer
actions: Open an appeal case on the date the appeal is received and confirm the claimant had at least 60 days from the adverse determination to file it.
Assign a reviewer who is neither the original decision-maker nor that person's subordinate, and record the segregation on the case.
Where the denial involved medical judgement, consult a health care professional with appropriate training who was not consulted on the initial denial, and record that consultant's identity.
Give the claimant, on request and free of charge, all documents, records and information relevant to the claim before the decision is made.
Decide inside the appeal clock and issue the determination with the §502(a) civil action statement.
checklist.done: every appeal is decided inside its clock by a segregated reviewer, with an independent medical consultant where medical judgement was involved.

checklist.step: Attach the evidence artifact to every calendar entry before closing it
actions: For each closed calendar entry attach the named artifact — EFAST2 acknowledgement receipt, SAR distribution log, SPD delivery record, determination letter with delivery proof.
Record the actual completion date on the entry alongside the due date so the timeliness gap is computed and stored, not inferred later.
Reject any closure request with no artifact attached and return it to the owner the same day.
Run a weekly report of entries closed in the last seven days with no artifact and clear it to zero.
checklist.done: no calendar entry is closed without its named evidence artifact and a stored actual-completion date.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to the obligation register each quarter
actions: Extract the obligation register and the calendar entries for the quarter and match them plan by plan.
List any register row with no calendar entry for a plan and any calendar entry with no register row behind it.
Re-read the eCFR text for any citation flagged as amended since the last review and update the day count on the register and every generated entry.
Add obligations arising from plan changes in the quarter — new plans, mergers, terminations, benefit changes — and generate their entries.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the reconciled register version.
checklist.done: the calendar and the obligation register reconcile with no unmatched rows either way, and the approved register version is dated.

checklist.step: Apply EBSA disaster or emergency relief to the clocks when it is issued
actions: Monitor EBSA news releases, Disaster Relief Notices and Compliance Assistance Releases for extensions to claim, appeal, COBRA or filing deadlines.
Assess which plans, claim categories and geographic areas the relief actually covers and write the scope determination.
Instruct the Business Systems Analyst to adjust the affected clocks in the case management configuration with an effective-date-bounded rule, not a blanket switch.
Notify affected claimants of the extended deadline where the relief requires it and retain the notice.
Record the relief, its scope and its expiry date on the obligation register so the clocks revert automatically.
checklist.done: every applicable relief has a written scope determination, a date-bounded clock adjustment and a recorded expiry that returns the clocks to normal.

checklist.step: Report calendar and claims timeliness to the Retirement Committee
actions: Publish the period dashboard: obligations due, completed on time, completed late with day counts, and open past due, split by plan.
Publish claims timeliness by category — urgent care, pre-service, post-service, disability, pension — with the count decided outside the clock.
Show every deemed-exhaustion event under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) and the litigation exposure it creates.
Record the committee's directed actions with owners and due dates in the minutes.
checklist.done: committee minutes record on-time rates by obligation and claim category, every deemed-exhaustion event, and directed actions with owners.

checklist.step: Remediate breached clocks and calendar failures at root cause
actions: For every breached claim clock, confirm with Legal Counsel whether the claimant is deemed to have exhausted administrative remedies and record the position on the case.
Complete the determination immediately regardless of the breach, and notify the claimant of their appeal and civil action rights.
Assign a root cause — intake logged late, wrong claim category, extension notice issued late, staffing gap, medical consultant unavailable — and a process owner.
Where the cause is a configuration defect, raise a change with the Business Systems Analyst and re-test the clock before closing the issue.
Set a remediation date and carry the item into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
checklist.done: every breach has a counsel position on deemed exhaustion, a completed determination, a root cause, an owner and a retest commitment.

checklist.step: Archive the calendar and claim timeliness evidence under ERISA retention
actions: Export the period's calendar with due dates, completion dates and evidence links and file it under the plan year.
Archive claim and appeal case files with received dates, extension notices, determination letters and delivery proof.
Apply the 6-year ERISA §107 retention label, and the longer §209 label on any record bearing on an individual's benefit entitlement.
Confirm the index makes records retrievable by plan number, claimant identifier, claim category and determination date.
checklist.done: the calendar export and claim case files are archived with the correct retention labels and are retrievable by plan, claimant and determination date.

testing.step: Build the population of calendar obligations and decided claims
actions: Extract every calendar entry with a due date inside the test period, with plan, obligation, owner, due date and completion date.
Extract every claim and appeal decided in the period from the case management tool with received date, category and determination date.
Add claims closed as withdrawn or abandoned so cases cannot be removed from the population by reclassification.
Reconcile the case counts to the claim system's volume report and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: the obligation and claim populations are extracted, reconciled to system volume reports and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the calendar to the independent statutory obligation inventory
actions: Build an independent obligation list from eCFR and the plan documents rather than from the maintained register.
Match it to the calendar per plan and list every obligation with no calendar entry — a missing entry is a control failure even where the underlying task was done.
Compare the day count on each entry to the current regulatory text and flag any stale day count.
Confirm any plan-specific commitment shorter than the regulatory minimum is the date actually calendared.
testing.done: the calendar is reconciled to an independently built obligation list with every missing entry and stale day count listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the timeliness sample
actions: Take 100% of urgent care claims, 100% of claims where an extension was applied, and 100% of appeals.
Take a seeded random sample of 40 remaining claims stratified across group health, disability, pension and life.
Take a seeded random sample of 25 calendar entries closed in the period.
Record the seed, population sizes, selection date and stratification rationale so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all urgent care claims, extended claims and appeals in full.

testing.step: Recompute each claim clock from the received date
actions: For each sampled claim take the received date from the source document — postmark, portal timestamp or fax header — not the system field.
Recompute the statutory due date from the category: 72 hours urgent care, 15 days pre-service, 30 days post-service, 45 days disability, 90 days pension.
Compare to the determination date on the letter and compute days early or late for every case.
Confirm the claim category assigned matches the claim's actual nature — a miscategorised urgent care claim decided in 30 days is a breach, not a pass.
testing.done: every sampled claim has an independently recomputed due date from a source-document received date and a days early/late figure.

testing.step: Test every extension for a valid, timely written notice
actions: For each extended claim, open the extension notice and compare its send date to the expiry of the original period.
Confirm the notice states the special circumstances and the date by which a decision would be rendered.
Where information was requested from the claimant, confirm at least 45 days were given and that the tolling period recorded matches the request and response dates.
Treat any extension without a notice sent before the original expiry as a breach of the original clock, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every extension is supported by a notice evidenced as sent before the original period expired, with the tolling period independently verified.

testing.step: Test adverse determination content against the regulation
actions: For each sampled denial read the determination letter against 29 CFR 2560.503-1(g): specific reason, specific plan provisions, additional material needed, appeal procedure and time limits.
Confirm the §502(a) civil action statement appears on the final adverse determination.
Confirm any internal rule or medical necessity basis is either stated or offered free on request.
Confirm delivery proof exists and treat a letter with no evidenced delivery as not issued.
testing.done: every sampled denial letter carries all required content elements, the §502(a) statement where required, and evidenced delivery.

testing.step: Test appeal reviewer segregation and independent medical consultation
actions: For each appeal compare the appeal reviewer to the initial decision-maker and to that person's reporting line in the HR org data.
Where medical judgement was involved, confirm a health care professional was consulted, that they were not consulted on the initial denial, and that their identity is recorded.
Confirm the claimant was given, on request and free of charge, the documents relevant to the claim before the appeal decision.
Treat any appeal decided by the original decision-maker or a subordinate as a fail.
testing.done: every appeal is evidenced as decided by a segregated reviewer with an independent medical consultant recorded where medical judgement applied.

testing.step: Verify the evidence artifact behind every sampled calendar closure
actions: Open each of the 25 sampled calendar entries and confirm the named evidence artifact is attached and matches the obligation.
Compare the artifact's own date — acknowledgement timestamp, distribution log date, letter date — to the recorded completion date.
Flag any entry closed with a placeholder, a screenshot without a date, or an artifact dated after the due date.
Recompute the on-time verdict for each sampled entry from the artifact date rather than the recorded status.
testing.done: every sampled entry has a dated artifact matching its obligation and an on-time verdict recomputed from the artifact date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with plan, claim or obligation reference, the clock breached, days late and the consequence.
Assign a root cause — intake logged late, miscategorised claim, late extension notice, staffing gap, stale calendar day count, missing evidence artifact — and an owner.
For every breached claim clock, record the Legal Counsel position on deemed exhaustion under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) and any litigation notification made.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with days late, a root cause, an owner, a deemed-exhaustion position where relevant, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the calendar and claims timeliness test
actions: Compute the on-time rate by claim category and by obligation type against the stated 100% clock-accuracy threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the clock recomputations and artifact verifications behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no calendar entry and adjudicated no sampled claim, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Retirement Committee and the Audit Committee, including every deemed-exhaustion event, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with on-time rates by category, a stated conclusion and a dated committee reporting reference is filed in the repository.
